Fujairah to host WFCC Grand Prix Final, with world's best solvers and composers
rubriker._rss_content: The Grand Final of the WFCC Fujairah Grand Prix 2025–2026 will take place from 27 to 30 November in Fujairah, bringing together leading chess solvers for the conclusion of the series’ inaugural cycle. The finalists will compete across six solving rounds for a €30,000 prize fund, while an accompanying composing tournament will add another dimension, with the solvers themselves voting for the best original problems and studies used in the event. | Photo: Fujairah Chess & Culture Club / FIDE

rubriker.title: Review: Libiszewski's Chigorin Defence – Calculated Risk against 1.d4 d5 2.c4
rubriker._rss_content: "The Chigorin Defence is an opening that brings back romantic chess memories for me. As a teenager, I played it for a few years. More precisely, between 1999 and 2001, as the Mega Database reminds me with unerring accuracy – a quarter of a century ago!" says Hannes Langrock. He is an editor at a publishing house specialising in fiction and an International Master. He lives in Leipzig and plays for ESV Nickelhütte-Aue. Here he reviews Libiszewski's latest course, which brought back a number of memories. | Photos: ChessBase

rubriker.title: KazChess Masters: Dubov moves ahead with consecutive wins
rubriker._rss_content: Daniil Dubov has taken the sole lead at the KazChess Masters in Almaty after scoring consecutive wins in rounds five and six. The Russian grandmaster stands on 4½/6, half a point ahead of Shamsiddin Vokhidov and Denis Lazavik. Remarkably, the same three players - Dubov, Vokhidov and Mahammad Muradli - won their games in the last two rounds. Early leaders Edgar Mamedov and Denis Makhnev are now a point behind Dubov. | Photo: Niki Riga / FIDE

rubriker.title: The amazing story of Peter Giannatos and the Charlotte Chess Center
rubriker._rss_content: Twelve years ago, a college student in Charlotte with an economics degree and no business plan asked his local chess community for $10,000 to open a chess club. They gave him $30,000. Today the Charlotte Chess Center teaches 2,500 children a week, runs more rated tournaments than there are days in the year, and hosts Judit Polgar, Peter Leko and Boris Gelfand as camp trainers. Sagar Shah travelled to Charlotte for the Daniel Naroditsky Memorial and sat down with founder Peter Giannatos to understand exactly how it was built. | All photos: Courtesy of Peter Giannatos and the Charlotte Chess Center

rubriker.title: XXXI Torneo San Andrés – Azkoitia 2026
rubriker._rss_content: El tradicional Torneo de San Andrés de Azkoitia celebrará su 31.ª edición el 28 de noviembre con una novedad importante: el traslado al frontón Gurea debido a la convocatoria electoral. La competición mantendrá su formato habitual de nueve rondas de blitz a 3+2, con numerosos premios por clasificación, Elo, edad y categorías especiales. La organización espera completar un aforo máximo de 189 participantes.
